@copilot Update this PR directly in open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation on its existing head renovate/main-major-spring-core. Keep the branch assigned by GitHub Copilot cloud agent; do not rename it or create a replacement branch. If GitHub creates a platform-assigned follow-up branch, keep it.

The user's decision is to update the benchmark to current dependencies rather than retaining a Spring 5 compile-only pin. This PR upgrades benchmark-overhead's test and startupHelper compile-only spring-webmvc from 5.3.3 to 7.1.0, but its Petclinic workload is still an old Boot 2.4.2/Spring 5 application. Modernize that workload and the directly related benchmark integration so the helper is compiled, tested, and actually executed against a consistent current supported Spring/Boot stack. Use the latest stable compatible releases available, not prereleases. Do not expand into repository-wide dependency upgrades unrelated to this workload.

Inspect benchmark-overhead/build.gradle.kts, Dockerfile.petclinic, src/startupHelper/java/io/opentelemetry/startup/PetclinicStartupUptimeResponseAdvice.java, src/startupHelper/resources/META-INF/spring.factories, src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/startup/PetclinicStartupFixture.java and its tests, AgentStartupBenchmark.java, other Petclinic benchmark callers, and the image/startup benchmark workflows. Upgrade the pinned Petclinic source and required build/runtime JDKs and database dependencies to current compatible releases. Account for modern Boot auto-configuration registration, launcher class/package and executable-JAR layout, and any actual Petclinic API, profile, or schema changes instead of assuming the old contracts still hold. Update directly related documentation.

Preserve benchmark meaning: the helper remains benchmark-only and must not bundle Spring; its advice leaves the response body unchanged and emits the JVM uptime/version headers only for the seeded-owner readiness GET. Seed and validate a known database record before measured launches, and retain equivalent workload and measurement semantics. Keep source and container inputs reproducible with verified immutable pins. Do not invent an image digest or leave the fixture pointing at the old Spring 5 image while claiming the upgrade is delivered. If a rebuilt GHCR image must be published outside your permissions, report that precise blocker and the required publication/repinning step rather than silently substituting unverified inputs.

Add focused coverage for changed integration contracts and exercise the real upgraded Petclinic startup workload where feasible, including helper discovery, readiness response/body and headers, and relevant benchmark configurations. Run the narrowest formatting task directly before relevant tests. Do not post replies to human reviewers or edit the PR title/description; the coordinating session will handle metadata separately. Report what was actually verified and any delivery blockers.

replies.body: Updated the Petclinic benchmark stack and fixture for Spring Boot 4.1.2/Spring Petclinic 4.0.2, JDK 25, PostgreSQL 18, modern Boot 4 launcher/auto-configuration, and directly related documentation/tests. Committed as `36f329ea`.

threads.body: Using mutable `latest` lets later image publications change the application/JVM used by archived startup reruns and daily overhead measurements, making workload changes look like agent regressions. Pin the upgraded application image by digest and align the reported image metadata and documentation with that reference. The same issue occurs in `benchmark-overhead/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/containers/PetClinicRestContainer.java:53`.

replies.body: Addressed in 128523a938e2a39560cd0bea1dabb8c339061340 by narrowing this PR to the image definition. Both consumers retain their previous fixed image references, and the added `latest` publication tag is removed. Switching consumers to the upgraded image's verified digest will happen in the separately planned integration PR after publication.

threads.body: The Temurin JRE image does not provide `jcmd`, but `AgentStartupBenchmark.sample()` invokes it to dump the mandatory startup profile, and `OverheadTests` invokes it to start/stop recordings. Petclinic can reach readiness and produce timing samples, then fail during profiling; the overhead workload also cannot produce its JFR data. Please use a pinned JDK runtime image, or otherwise provide the matching diagnostic tools in the final stage.

replies.body: Committed `b45fc442`: the runtime now uses a verified, digest-pinned Temurin 25 JDK image, and `jcmd -h` succeeds in it. The upgraded Petclinic image still cannot be safely pinned here: GHCR `latest` resolves to the 2022 image (`sha256:5039f3e67b4dd355970686a3dd1e07d32556ebedf771d1472ac5bf32277af0a9`), while a local build of the upgraded image failed Maven Central TLS validation and this environment cannot publish the rebuilt image. I did not replace the two references with a stale image or an invented digest. Publication of the upgraded image and repinning both consumers plus metadata/README remain required.

threads.body: The daily workflow restores historical results, then `CsvPersister` appends measurements from this upgraded application/JVM/database stack to the same `results/release/results.csv`, without a stack identifier. This mixes workloads that the PR explicitly identifies as non-comparable. Start a separate versioned results series, or add a machine-readable stack boundary that downstream comparisons honor.

replies.body: Addressed in 128523a938e2a39560cd0bea1dabb8c339061340 by keeping the current benchmark workload unchanged in this image-only PR. The PostgreSQL and application-image consumer upgrades are reverted, so existing CSV series continue measuring the same stack. The later integration PR will switch workloads and start a new versioned results directory while preserving historical CSVs.
